run.procedureSummary:
Start: x0=(3,6,6,2,2,1), s=0, all flags INACTIVE. Each cycle does five steps, and each step finishes across the whole vector before the next starts.
1. Load: add the cycle's row of b to x. No bounds are enforced at this step.
2. Projection sweep (Gauss-Seidel, i=1 to 6): if x_i>c_i, set x_i=c_i and add the excess to x_{i+1} before visiting it. The excess from position 6 goes to s.
3. Active-set update on the projected x: an INACTIVE component becomes ACTIVE if x_i>=u_i. An ACTIVE component becomes INACTIVE if x_i<=d_i. Otherwise the flag stays. Every flip is logged.
4. Jacobi shed: compute every amount from the same pre-shed x, using the flags just set. INACTIVE: floor(x_i/4) goes to s. ACTIVE: floor(x_i/2) goes to x_{i-1}, and position 1's share goes to s. There is no projection afterwards.
5. Penalty: if sum(x)>38 (strictly), each x_i becomes floor(x_i/2) and the removed part, x_i-floor(x_i/2), goes to s. The cycle is noted.

openPoints.point: Penalty rounding: the write-up says to halve with floor and book what came off to s. It could also mean removing floor(x/2).
openPoints.assumption: New x_i = floor(x_i/2), and the amount booked to s is x_i - floor(x_i/2) (that is, ceil(x_i/2)). This conserves the total.
The shed uses the flags just updated in step 3 of the same cycle. The final states are the flags after cycle 5 step 3, since no later step changes them.
It is the sum of the six x components only. Slack s is not included.

openPoints.point: Boundary case in cycle 5: the 1-norm after the shed is exactly 38
openPoints.assumption: The rule says strictly above, so the penalty does not fire in cycle 5.

openPoints.point: End values over their bounds (x2=10>8, x4=7>6)
openPoints.assumption: They are left as they are, because the write-up says no projection follows the cycle 5 shed.
Only the upper bounds c bind. No component goes negative at any point.

run.balanceCheck: Starting 1-norm 20 + everything loaded 94 = 114. Final 1-norm 38 + s 76 = 114. The two sides match.
